definitions.explanation: Indicates exclusion of what precedes it.

examples.japanese: {日曜日|にちようび}{以外|いがい}は{毎日|まいにち}{働|はたら}いています。
examples.english: I work every day except Sunday.

examples.japanese: これ{以外|いがい}に{方法|ほうほう}はない。
examples.english: There's no method other than this.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}{以外|いがい}{誰|だれ}もいなかった。
examples.english: There was no one besides me.

examples.japanese: {肉|にく}{以外|いがい}は{何|なん}でも{食|た}べます。

notes:
{以外|いがい} means 'other than' or 'except.'

Grammar patterns:
- [noun]{以外|いがい}: other than [noun]
- [noun]{以外|いがい}に: besides [noun], other than [noun]
- [noun]{以外|いがい}の[noun]: [noun] other than ~

Note: Unlike English, {以外|いがい} comes AFTER the thing being excluded.

Similar expressions:
- 〜{以外|いがい} vs. 〜の{他|ほか}に: Both mean 'besides,' but {以外|いがい} emphasizes exclusion, while {他|ほか}に focuses on addition.
- 〜を{除|のぞ}いて: more formal way to say 'except'
